text: Omar, I am on the Cedar night desk. The lot light by the loading door is out. I can still see the step.
Seattle night board is quiet. I am here for the trailer page when you have one. No rush while you are still counting.
Coffee is on. The pot from the day shift was empty. I started a new one.
Our pot is the same story. The night supervisor mug was in the sink. I washed it.
Door alarm chirped once when I came in and then settled. I am not calling facilities for a single chirp.
If it chirps again, write it on the sheet. Do not stop a count for a door.
The body is not finished. I am still on the detail rows. Header is written. Trailer is not.
I will not archive a trailer you have not written. Cascade can wait for the page that actually left.
Thermostat in the file room is low. I put my coat on the chair. I am not changing the dial.
Our floor is warm. Different building. I only need the page, not the temperature.
Radio in the back is a weather report. Roads into the clinic are clear. I turned it down.
Seattle rain, nothing on the bridges. Ordinary night.
Janitor came through for the bins. I asked him to leave the tray table. He did.
Our janitor is on two. I have the records cage to myself.
Sandwich from the day fridge. I am eating it over the sink so the count sheet stays clean.
I have a bag of crackers. This is not a dinner conversation. Count when you are ready.
First pass of the body is 40 detail rows. I am going to count them again before I touch the trailer.
Forty is your pass, not mine. I do not replace a clinic count from Seattle.
Copier in the hall has a jam from the afternoon. I am not clearing it. The trailer page can be the carbon I already use.
Carbon is fine. I archive the trailer, not a fresh photocopy, if that is what you set aside.
The header carries the file id for tonight's send. I have not released the file. The body is still the thing I am willing to stand behind, or it is not, and I am not done deciding that.
Understood. No release, no trailer page on my desk. I am walking the cage while you recount.
Second pass is also 40. I wrote the body count on the sheet without erasing the first pass. They match each other. That is only the body.
Two passes of the body. I still do not have a trailer count. I am not going to invent one so the archive looks complete.
Pencil snapped. I am using the spare from the cup. Same sheet.
A truck just went by our loading dock. Not yours. Ignore me.
Hand soap in the file-room sink is empty. I am not leaving the count to find a refill.
There is a spare carton in our closet if you ever need one. Not tonight.
While I was moving the old stack to reach the release stamp, I saw cedar-2025-05-25-45 again. I set that stack back. I am not opening it tonight.
Old stack stays old. I am still waiting on tonight.
The day note on the blotter says the exterior light bulb is in the bottom drawer. I am leaving the bulb for morning.
Morning can have the bulb. Did the second body pass stay at the same number after you moved the stack?
Yes. Body count is still 40. I have not written the trailer yet. Moving paper did not add a row.
Good. I had a caller for the Seattle night line about a parking voucher. Not your clinic. I sent them to the day desk message.
Our phone has been quiet. One ring, wrong number, a pharmacy in town. I told them this is the clinic night desk and hung up.
I am putting the archive folder on the chair so I do not have to hunt for it later. The folder is empty until your page arrives.
I am writing the trailer now. The file id in the trailer is the same string as the header. I checked them against each other before I counted.
Same string is the check you do. I do not rewrite it from here.
Trailer count is 40. Body count is 40. I read them aloud once. They are the same integer. That is the release comparison on my sheet. It is not a sentence for a desk in another city.
I hear two forties. I am not telling Vancouver anything. I want the trailer page after the file has actually left.
It has not left. I am at the send step and I have not pressed it. The folder the day staff watch is still the folder they had. Give me the next few minutes.
Take the minutes. I am refilling my water. The cooler gulps.
The stamp pad is dry on one corner. I turned it. The trailer page is readable.
Readable is what I need. A smudged count is how morning arguments start, and I am not starting one.
A branch knocked the window. Wind, not a person. I looked. The lot is empty.
Our windows are quiet. Send when the sheet is the sheet you mean.
The file is going now. File id cedar-2027-01-11. Trailer is the last record. Body count 40, trailer count 40. I am writing the time I actually sent it on the night sheet.
Landed on my side as a notice that a file left the clinic. I do not have the trailer page in my hand yet. Do not tell me the notice is the page.

The page is the carbon of the trailer I just wrote. I am setting it in the slot your office picks up. Header time and the time I wrote on the sheet are both on the paper. I am not finishing which zone a reader should use.
I will take the carbon as the trailer of the file that left. I will not pick a zone for you. I will not change 40 to another count.
The send is the send. I am not backdating the sheet to match a sentence someone said this afternoon. The real send time stays the time I wrote.
Archive copy will show your trailer count and your file id. Cascade's night book does not become the clinic's night book because I hole-punch the page.
Hole-punch it. The tray here still has the sheet. If morning asks me whether a spoken visit is in the file, I will answer from the rows, not from this chat.
I am not asking you to answer a visit in this chat. I have the trailer page in the cage now. File id matches what you said. Count matches what you said.
Then you have the trailer of the file that landed. You do not have a ruling from me about a screen, and I do not have a ruling from you about the sheet.
Agreed that we do not have that. The cage has a page. That is the whole of what I came for.
I am wiping the count table. Pencil shavings in the bin. The release stamp goes back in the drawer.
I walked the page to the night shelf. It is behind the Monday divider, loose, not clipped to another clinic.
Good. Leave it loose. A clip would look like I attached it to something else.
Loose it is. I am making tea. The kettle here takes forever.
I will rinse the coffee pot and sit the night sheet where the morning clerk can see the file id, the body count, and the trailer count.
My copy is filed. If the counts ever disagree with yours, I will bring you the page. They do not disagree tonight.
Tonight's file has left. The trailer is written. The sheet shows the send I actually made. I am not turning that into anything larger before I lock the door.
